# Validating scenarios (Go)

A scenario's `Up`/`Down` is ordinary Go, but its `Down` is easy to get subtly wrong, so validate every scenario against a real database before it reaches production. The Go SDK ships no dry-run helper. You validate the way the platform will hit you: drive `autonoma.HandleRequest` through a full `up` then `down` cycle in a `*_test.go`, signing each request the same way the platform does. This exercises the whole envelope - HMAC verification, teardown-token signing on `up` and verification on `down` - with no HTTP server involved.

Two build-time guards catch the coarsest mistakes before any test runs: `autonoma.DefineScenario` panics if `Name` is empty or `Up` is nil, so a malformed scenario fails at process start.

## Sign the request, then run the cycle

Every request carries an `x-signature` header: the HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body, hex-encoded, keyed with the shared secret. `autonoma.SignBody(body, secret)` computes exactly that, so a small test helper builds a signed `HandlerRequest`:

```go
// scenarios/validate_test.go
package scenarios

import (
    "encoding/json"
    "testing"

    "github.com/autonoma-ai/sdk/sdks/go/v2/autonoma"
)

const (
    sharedSecret  = "test-shared-secret"
    signingSecret = "test-signing-secret" // must differ from sharedSecret
)

func signed(t *testing.T, body map[string]any) autonoma.HandlerRequest {
    t.Helper()
    raw, err := json.Marshal(body)
    if err != nil {
        t.Fatalf("marshal request body: %v", err)
    }
    str := string(raw)
    return autonoma.HandlerRequest{
        Body:    str,
        Headers: map[string]string{"x-signature": autonoma.SignBody(str, sharedSecret)},
    }
}
```

Then run each scenario end to end: `up` to get a `teardownToken`, then `down` with that token. Point your DB client at a real (test) database first, because `Up`/`Down` run the real creation and deletion code.

```go
func TestScenarios(t *testing.T) {
    config := &autonoma.HandlerConfig{
        SharedSecret:  sharedSecret,
        SigningSecret: signingSecret,
        Scenarios:     All, // the same slice you pass to GinHandler
    }

    for _, s := range config.Scenarios {
        t.Run(s.Name, func(t *testing.T) {
            up := autonoma.HandleRequest(config, signed(t, map[string]any{
                "action":    "up",
                "scenario":  map[string]any{"name": s.Name},
                "testRunId": "validate-" + s.Name,
            }))
            if up.Status != 200 {
                t.Fatalf("up failed: %d %v", up.Status, up.Body)
            }

            token, _ := up.Body["teardownToken"].(string)

            down := autonoma.HandleRequest(config, signed(t, map[string]any{
                "action":        "down",
                "teardownToken": token,
                "testRunId":     "validate-" + s.Name,
            }))
            if down.Status != 200 || down.Body["ok"] != true {
                t.Fatalf("down failed: %d %v", down.Status, down.Body)
            }
        })
    }
}
```

```bash
go test ./autonoma/ -v          # the SDK's own suite
go test ./scenarios/ -v         # your validation test
```

## Reading the outcome

`HandleRequest` never panics for a scenario error; it returns a `HandlerResponse{ Status, Body }`. A failure surfaces as a non-200 status with an error envelope in `Body`:

| `Status` | `Body["code"]` | What it means |
|----------|----------------|---------------|
| 200 | (none; `teardownToken` on `up`, `ok: true` on `down`) | The cycle succeeded. |
| 400 | `UNKNOWN_ENVIRONMENT` / `INVALID_BODY` | The scenario name is not registered, or the request is missing `scenario.name` / `teardownToken`. |
| 403 | `INVALID_TEARDOWN_TOKEN` | The `down` token was signed with a different `SigningSecret` or tampered with. |
| 500 | `INTERNAL_ERROR` | `Up` or `Down` returned an `error`; `Body["error"]` is that error's message. |

## The testcontainers harness

The reliable way to validate locally is a real Postgres in Docker (for example `github.com/testcontainers/testcontainers-go/modules/postgres`). Start the container in `TestMain`, point your DB client at its connection string, run your schema/migrations, then run the loop above over your whole `All` slice in one test.

## The fix loop

Validation is iterative, especially the first time you write a scenario:

1. Run the test.
2. If a scenario fails, read `Status` and `Body["error"]` / `Body["code"]`.
3. Fix the scenario code and re-run.
4. Repeat until every scenario returns 200 on both `up` and `down`.

Common failures and fixes:

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---------|-------|-----|
| `Unique constraint failed ... email` inside an `INTERNAL_ERROR` | A unique value was not seeded from `TestRunID`, so two runs collide | Derive it with `autonoma.UniqueEmail`/`UniqueSlug`/`UniqueID` from `ctx.TestRunID`. |
| `INTERNAL_ERROR` at the `down` request | `Down` read a handle `Up` never put in `Teardown`, or a nil map assertion, or deleted in the wrong order | Return every id `Down` needs from `Up` as `Teardown`, assert types defensively, and delete children before parents. |
| `INTERNAL_ERROR` at the `up` request | Provisioning code returned an `error` (missing required field, bad FK) | Fix the creation call; run the same code path your app uses in production. |
| panic at process start | `DefineScenario` got an empty `Name` or nil `Up` | Give the scenario a non-empty `Name` and a non-nil `Up`. |
